question: Does a two-decision online reservation search improve over a hand future-rollout portfolio when background workflows arrive without advance notice?
physics: Four irregular four-operation DAGs on three hosts, sequence-dependent setup, locks and power domains; three workflows announced at t=0 and one hidden until t=4..12 ms
primary: At each event, score up to 16 first actions with four hand continuations, then score second actions under top four first actions; at most 32 exact visible-workflow continuations per decision
matched_hand: Same current state and revealed DAGs, same four continuation rules and exact simulator, at most 32 one-decision continuations per decision
retry: If the primary fails, use four first actions chosen by diverse hand rules, including wait where feasible; score four continuations each, then use remaining cap on second actions. Run once on disjoint seeds with the same hand control and complete live replay.
weak_control: Immediate short-job dispatch with no future rollout
objective: Sum of all four workflow completion times; future background arrival is not visible to either planner
advancement_bar: At least 3% median paired gain over the matched hand portfolio and at least 12 of 16 wins on fresh qualification seeds
live: Replay every qualification arm in actual HeROsim with realized starts as reservations and actual staggered arrivals; audit every operation start, completion, host and setup event
scope_limit: Materialized live replay verifies physical execution but is not an online policy callback; the screen does not train or test a GNN
